جُدَرِىٌّ and جَدَرِىٌّ (S, Msb, K) [Small-pox;] certain pustules (Msb, K) in the body, (K,) which break forth (Msb, K) from the skin, full of water, and afterwards opening, (Msb,) and generating thick purulent matter; (K;) a well-known disease, that attacks people once during life. (TA.) ―
-b2- جُدَرِىُّ الأَرْضِ (tropical:) an appellation applied to Truffles (كَمْأَة), denoting disapprobation. (TA from a trad.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
